html:
Vasconia was the land of the Basque-speaking Vascones on both sides of the western Pyrenees, from the late 500s to the 1000s. It is on the map for 600 and 700.

The Basques held out against every larger power around them: the Franks to the north, the Visigoths to the south, and later the Muslim rulers of al-Andalus. The Franks set up a Duchy of Vasconia north of the mountains about 602, but its dukes often acted on their own. In 778 Basques ambushed the rearguard of Charlemagne's army at the pass of Roncevaux, the fight later sung in the Song of Roland.

South of the mountains the Basque lands gave rise to the Kingdom of Pamplona, later Navarre. North of them the name Vasconia became Gascony.
sum: Vasconia was the land of the Basque-speaking Vascones on both sides of the western Pyrenees, from the late 500s to the 1000s. It is on the map for 600 and 700.
